title: Enterprise Onboarding, QBR & Health Check Playbook
author: Maya Thompson
body:
Overview:
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s standardized enterprise onboarding process, support escalation path, integration checklist, known issues and workarounds, and Quarterly Business Review (QBR) / health check templates. It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), and Support teams running enterprise-wide onboarding and ongoing account health programs.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-value for enterprise customers during first 90 days.
- Ensure consistent handoff between Sales -> SE -> CS -> Support.
- Provide a repeatable QBR and health check cadence measuring latency, cost, reliability and feature adoption.
- Define escalation paths and runbooks for common production issues.

Ownership and RACI:
- CS Manager: overall runbook owner, QBR lead.
- Solutions Engineering: integration and onboarding technical lead.
- Support (SRE liaison): incident triage and page-on-call ownership.
- Product: roadmap/feature updates for QBRs.
- Customer Success: day-to-day contact, adoption campaigns.

High-level Onboarding Timeline (90-day plan):
1) Pre-installation (Sales -> SE handoff)
   - Deliverables: Signed contract, SSO/KMS requirements, network allowlist, initial model/version choices.
   - Technical checks: customer provides preferred VPC or IP ranges, KMS key ARN (if Private), and TLS certificates (if required).
2) Week 0: Kickoff (Day 0–7)
   - Kickoff call agenda: introductions, success criteria (SLOs), data privacy, timeline.
   - Assign runbook owners and create shared project board (Jira/Asana).
3) Week 1-2: Integration & Test Environment
   - SE to provision sandbox / Dedicated reservation per contract.
   - Integration checklist (see section below).
   - Demo sample calls: text generation, chat flows, embeddings, streaming.
4) Week 3-6: Pilot & Performance Validation
   - Run synthetic load tests: p95 latency target and token cost validation.
   - Collect sample prompts, evaluate quality/regression with Redwood Optimize.
   - Address quantization or model variant recommendations.
5) Week 6-10: Production Cutover
   - Configure routing policies, autoscaling policies, and retries.
   - Conduct smoke test and initial production traffic ramp.
6) Week 10-90: Adoption, QBR Preparation, and Handoff to Success
   - Regular check-ins, usage reviews, QBR scheduling at 30/60/90 days.

Integration Checklist (technical):
- Authentication:
  - Confirm API key or OIDC/SSO mapping configured.
  - Confirm RBAC roles for project-level access.
- Network & Security:
  - For Private: validate VPC peering, egress rules, and KMS/HSM integration.
  - Ensure outbound allowlist for Redwood control plane IPs (if applicable).
- Model & Data:
  - Confirm model versions to serve, tokenization expectations, and any fine-tuned weights.
  - Verify prompt templates and schema for function/tool calling.
- Observability & Alerts:
  - Ensure customer has read-only access to Redwood Console dashboards (latency, cost).
  - Configure alerting thresholds in our monitoring export (PagerDuty, Slack).
- Compliance:
  - Verify required audit log retention, legal-approved data residency.

Sample Integration Test Cases (run by SE):
- Latency baseline: 1k request sample; measure p50/p90/p95 for target payloads.
- Throughput validation: 5-10 minute sustained throughput to match contracted RPS.
- Failure modes: simulate KV cache miss, sudden spike, and backend GPU OOM.
- Security tests: verify SSO auth flow, token rotation, and permission denial cases.

Escalation Path & Triage Matrix:
- Tier 0: Customer Success/SE triage
  - Low-impact usability questions, onboarding checklist items. Response SLA: 24 business hours.
- Tier 1: Redwood Support (1st-line)
  - Product bugs, minor regressions, credentials, dashboard access. Response SLA: 4 business hours.
- Tier 2: SRE / Eng (second-line)
  - Degraded performance, model inference errors, increased error rates. Response SLA: 2 hours for P1; 8 hours for P2.
- Tier 3: Incident Response & Engineering
  - P0 outages, data loss, security incidents. Immediate paging via PagerDuty.

Escalation Contacts (default):
- CS Oncall (business hours): cs-oncall@redwood.ai
- Support Pager (24/7): support-pager@redwood.ai (routes to PagerDuty)
- SRE Oncall: sre-oncall@redwood.ai
- Security Incident Response: sec-incident@redwood.ai

Priority Definitions and SLAs:
- P0 (Outage): Service unavailable or major data loss. Immediate page. Target TTR: 1 hour initial containment.
- P1 (Severe): Significant degradation causing customer-visible failure (high error rate or >50% latency SLO breach). Page SRE. Target TTR: 4 hours.
- P2 (Medium): Functional but degraded or correctness regressions (quality issues). Response within 8 business hours.
- P3 (Low): Feature requests, documentation issues. Response within 3 business days.

Incident Runbook Examples (common scenarios):
1) High p95 latency for text-generation endpoints
  - Verify recent deploys: git tags, release notes.
  - Check model routing: confirm requests are hitting intended model variant.
  - Inspect GPU utilization and queue depth in Redwood Console.
  - If queue growth > 20% over baseline, enable burst autoscaling or failover to lower-latency variant.
  - Notify customer and document mitigation steps in incident ticket.
2) Increased 5xx errors for embedding endpoint
  - Confirm API keys/auth.
  - Check model VM health and recent kernel crashes.
  - If node OOMs, escalate to SRE to repro and collect core dumps.
  - Apply automatic fallback to standby model if configured.

Known Issues & Workarounds (living table):
- Issue: Occasional memory pressure with long context windows (>65k tokens).
  - Impact: Elevated latency and occasional rejections.
  - Workaround: Use model with chunked context or enable KV prefix caching. SE to recommend quantization profile.
- Issue: SSO SAML assertion timeouts for certain IdPs
  - Impact: Intermittent login failures for admin users.
  - Workaround: Increase assertion lifetime on IdP or configure Redwood session refresh.
- Issue: Model quality regression after a rolling release
  - Impact: Output correctness drop on specific prompt sets.
  - Workaround: Roll back to prior model version and run Redwood Optimize evals; create regression ticket with Model Onboarding.

QBR & Health Check Framework:
- Cadence: Initial 30/60/90-day reviews, then quarterly for enterprise customers (QBR).
- Attendees: Customer executive sponsor, CS lead, SE technical owner, Product manager (as needed), SRE liaison.
- Pre-QBR deliverables (to customer 7 days prior): current usage dashboard link, cost breakdown, list of open tickets, action items log.

Standard QBR Agenda (60 minutes):
1) Introductions & objectives (5 min)
2) Adoption & Usage Trends (10 min)
  - Active routes, token consumption, cost per 1k tokens, feature adoption (streaming, function calls).
3) Reliability & Performance (15 min)
  - SLO compliance (monthly p99/p95/p50), incidents since last QBR, mitigation actions.
4) Roadmap & Product updates (10 min)
  - Upcoming model variants, quantization improvements, new console features.
5) Open action items & next steps (10 min)
6) Business outcomes & Success metrics review (10 min)

QBR Health Metrics (recommended KPIs):
- Availability: % successful requests (target >= 99.9% monthly).
- Latency: p95 for primary routes (target per contract e.g., <300ms for small payloads).
- Cost efficiency: $ per 1k tokens or $ per 1k embeddings (trend over quarter).
- Error rate: 5xx rate (target <0.1%).
- Model quality: Regression score on customer-held prompt set (pass/fail + delta).
- Adoption: Number of active endpoints, seats using the platform, percentage of traffic on optimized routes.

Templates and Artifacts (links to copyable templates):
- Onboarding checklist (CSV/Jira template)
- QBR slide deck template (PPTX)
- Health check dashboard export (JSON for Redwood Console)
- Incident postmortem template (Confluence page skeleton)

Post-Onboarding Handoff Checklist:
- All open integration tickets resolved or triaged with owners.
- Customer has access to billing and cost controls.
- Playbook for runbook triggers documented in their account.
- Recurring QBR schedule created in shared calendar.

Maintenance and Continuous Improvement:
- Quarterly review of playbook: CS leads to propose changes, collect feedback from SE and SRE.
- Regression triage: link to applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage for model-related regressions.
- Known issues owner: Support Engineering maintains the known issues table and updates workarounds.

Appendices:
A) Useful CLI snippets
- Curl example (text generation):
  curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY"
    -H "Content-Type: application/json"
    -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","input":"Tell me a joke."}'

B) Contact & Escalation Quick Reference
